institution: The University of Texas at Dallas
headline: Building a next-generation AI biomaterials workforce.
introduction: NEXABio brings together artificial intelligence, biomaterials, and computational research. Our CyberTraining pilot prepares undergraduate and graduate students to apply data-driven methods to the discovery and design of biomaterials.

heroImage.alt: 2D concept illustration of a polymer scaffold, a molecular chain, and a drug-delivery carrier beside a cell membrane.
heroImage.caption: AI + biomaterials · Conceptual illustration

overview: Through workshops, a summer bootcamp, and invited talks, students will connect polymer chemistry and biomaterials fundamentals with machine learning, high-performance computing, and reproducible research practices.

programImage.alt: Illustration of three students collaborating around a laptop and a biomaterial scaffold model.
programImage.caption: Student collaboration · Illustration

activities.title: CyberTraining Workshops
activities.description: Short lectures, guided coding exercises, and team-based mini-projects build computational skills progressively. Students work with real biomaterials datasets and connect AI methods with experimental questions.

activities.title: Summer Bootcamp
activities.description: An intensive introduction to AI-enabled biomaterials research, with practical exercises in scientific programming, machine learning, and computing workflows. Collaborative projects conclude with student presentations.

activities.title: Invited Talks
activities.format: In person or online · Every other week
activities.description: Researchers share developments in AI-driven biomaterials design, polymer discovery, drug delivery, and regenerative medicine. Discussions connect current research with workshop and bootcamp activities.

curriculumIntroduction: The proposed workshop curriculum progresses from foundations to practical research workflows. Topics combine AI methods with the chemical, physical, and biological questions that shape biomaterials design.

curriculum.title: Foundations of AI-driven biomaterials
curriculum.description: Biomaterials data, machine learning pipelines, and data preparation.

curriculum.title: Structure–property prediction
curriculum.description: Supervised learning, model evaluation, and benchmarking.

curriculum.title: Deep learning and multimodal data
curriculum.description: Neural networks for imaging, spectroscopy, and combined data sources.

curriculum.title: AI-driven biomaterials design
curriculum.description: Active learning, Bayesian optimization, and closed-loop design.

curriculum.title: Generative modeling
curriculum.description: Generative models for exploring candidate biomaterial structures.

curriculum.title: Computing for biomaterials research
curriculum.description: High-performance computing, job scheduling, and cloud workflows.

curriculum.title: Uncertainty-aware optimization
curriculum.description: Probabilistic modeling and design under uncertainty.

curriculum.title: Deployment and reproducibility
curriculum.description: Containers, workflow automation, and reproducible model pipelines.

curriculum.title: Student mini-project presentations
curriculum.description: Communicating methods, results, limitations, and research insights.

projects: Example projects include predicting drug and gene delivery properties, selecting candidate monomers for material design, and assessing the reliability of model predictions using open biomaterials datasets.

application.audience: The program is designed for undergraduate and graduate students in bioengineering, computer science, materials science, chemistry, and related fields. Participation is intended to include students at UT Dallas and other institutions.
application.experience: Students with different levels of computational experience are encouraged to explore the program. Final prerequisites and eligibility requirements will be published with the application.

resources.description: The project plans to share instructional materials, computational notebooks, dataset references, and reproducible workflows to support learning during the program and adoption by other institutions.
